t: This was Bedford College, founded in London in 1849 as the first higher education college for women in the United Kingdom. Its founder was Elizabeth Jesser Reid, a social reformer, anti-slavery activist and philanthropist, best remembered for starting it. In 1900 the college became part of the University of London, and it led the way in advancing women in higher education and public life. It turned fully coeducational in the 1960s, and in 1985 merged with Royal Holloway College.
